commit.message:
chore(tsconfig): centralize `lib` option in base config (#24558)

## Background

- our TypeScript configs drifted because `base.json` didn't set a `lib`
- so each package's config extended it
- many of those are ancient (e.g. `ES2018` in `ts-library.json`) even
though our min supported node version is Node 22

## Summary

- Set `"lib": ["ES2024", "dom", "dom.iterable"]` in
`tools/tsconfig/base.json`
- Node 22 supports everything in the ES2024 lib, so this is a safe
shared default.
- Remove per-config `lib` overrides from the shared configs
(`ts-library.json`, `react-library.json`) and from the packages and
examples that extend them.

commit.message:
fix(cohere): read response id from v2 chat responses (#24621)

## Background

Follow-up to #24574 (`fix(cohere): tolerate partial citations and usage
in
non-streaming responses`). Its Future Work section noted that
`doGenerate` read
`response.generation_id`, while Cohere's v2 chat response
(`components.schemas.ChatResponseV2`) has a required `id` and no
`generation_id`.
As a result, the provider's response id never reached `doGenerate`, and
streaming
(which reads the id from the `message-start` event) and non-streaming
disagreed.

## Summary

- `@ai-sdk/cohere`: the non-streaming chat response schema now accepts
`id`, and
`doGenerate` returns `response.id ?? response.generation_id ??
undefined`.
`generation_id` is the v1 chat field and v2 never returns it; the
fallback is
kept only for compatibility with proxies/mocks that still return it. It
is not
  used anywhere else in the provider, so no other behavior changes.
- Added regression tests for using `id`, preferring it over
`generation_id`,
falling back to `generation_id`, and returning `undefined` when both are
absent.
- Updated existing snapshots that expected the old `id: undefined`
behavior.
- Added a patch changeset for `@ai-sdk/cohere`.

## End-to-End Verification

Prerequisites: Node.js 22.13+, `pnpm` 12+, and a `COHERE_API_KEY`
available in
`examples/ai-functions/.env` (not included here). Secrets are loaded
only through
Node's `--env-file`, never sourced in the shell.

Setup and build from the checkout root, run before and after the change:

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=ai... --filter=@ai-sdk/cohere... --output-logs=errors-only
```

Both runs execute the script from `examples/ai-functions`, a workspace
member, so
`ai` and `@ai-sdk/cohere` resolve this checkout's locally built packages
through
the workspace links rather than published registry versions.

Reproduction script (`/tmp/repro-cohere-response-id/repro.mjs`, outside
the
checkout). `RAW=1` is a separate scratch step that calls the HTTP API
directly to
show the field name returned by Cohere:

```js
import { generateText, streamText } from 'ai';
import { cohere } from '@ai-sdk/cohere';

const model = cohere('command-a-03-2025');

if (process.env.RAW === '1') {
  const response = await fetch('https://api.cohere.com/v2/chat', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.COHERE_API_KEY}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      model: 'command-a-03-2025',
      messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Say hi in five words.' }],
      stream: false,
    }),
  });
  const body = await response.json();
  console.log('status:', response.status);
  console.log('top-level keys:', Object.keys(body).sort().join(', '));
  console.log('id:', body.id);
  console.log('generation_id:', body.generation_id);
  process.exit(0);
}

console.log('=== generateText ===');
const generated = await generateText({
  model,
  prompt: 'Say hi in five words.',
});
console.log('text:', JSON.stringify(generated.text));
console.log('response.id:', generated.response.id);

console.log('=== streamText ===');
const streamed = streamText({
  model,
  prompt: 'Say hi in five words.',
});
const streamedText = await streamed.text;
const streamedResponse = await streamed.response;
console.log('text:', JSON.stringify(streamedText));
console.log('response.id:', streamedResponse.id);
```

Scratch step proving the field name:

```bash
cd examples/ai-functions
RAW=1 node --env-file=.env --input-type=module < /tmp/repro-cohere-response-id/repro.mjs
```

```text
status: 200
top-level keys: finish_reason, id, message, usage
id: 8b93456c-2b06-4505-b135-fa49e7b7fc1b
generation_id: undefined
```

Before the fix:

```bash
cd examples/ai-functions
node --env-file=.env --input-type=module < /tmp/repro-cohere-response-id/repro.mjs
```

```text
=== generateText ===
text: "Hi there, how's it going?"
response.id: aitxt-srWwNAzJMCMYFimNNXCieY2u
=== streamText ===
text: "Hi there, how's it going?"
response.id: d53e0879-247d-4089-8380-aff3b54dfce6
```

`generateText` does not expose the missing provider id as `undefined`:
when
`result.response?.id` is absent it substitutes a generated `aitxt-...`
id
(`packages/ai/src/generate-text/generate-text.ts`). The baseline
therefore shows a
local fallback id that differs from the Cohere id returned by
`streamText`. The raw
request above confirms Cohere only returns `id`.

After the fix:

```text
=== generateText ===
text: "Hello, how are you?"
response.id: ca6fb289-9c88-46ae-8141-0c244c437aed
=== streamText ===
text: "Hello, how are you?"
response.id: f835c9a5-6788-4193-ac4c-892f72f430f4
```

Both calls now report the Cohere response id (a UUID). The provider flow
exercised
was `cohere('command-a-03-2025')` through `generateText` and
`streamText` with a
short text prompt. Tool-call and citation flows are not part of this
script;
regression tests cover the response id schema behavior with mocked
responses.

commit.message:
fix(provider/gateway): document oidc fallback in types and readme (#24557)

## Background

Developers and coding agents read the `@ai-sdk/gateway` source to learn
how it authenticates: whether a deployed Vercel Function needs an API
key, and which wins when both an API key and OIDC are available. The
package doesn't say. The `apiKey` JSDoc mentions only
`AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, and the README has no authentication guidance. The
answer lives in `getGatewayAuthToken()`.

## Summary

Document the existing precedence (`apiKey`, then `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`,
then the Vercel OIDC token resolved for each request) where people look:

- `GatewayProviderSettings.apiKey` JSDoc (this ends up in
`dist/index.d.ts`) now covers:
- the OIDC fallback: automatic on Vercel deployments, `vercel env pull`
or `vercel dev` locally;
  - precedence: a non-empty API key always wins, even if it's invalid;
- the failure: a `GatewayAuthenticationError` ("No authentication
provided") when no OIDC token is available either.
- `getGatewayAuthToken()` gets a doc comment listing the order and
noting the empty-string behavior: an empty string option or env var
falls through to OIDC, and a callback must return a non-empty key.
- The README gets a one-line auth comment in the Usage example and a
link to the authentication docs, within `README-3`.
- Patch changeset for `@ai-sdk/gateway`.

No behavior change.

## Verification

- `pnpm build` in `packages/gateway`: the new JSDoc is present in
`dist/index.d.ts`.
- `vitest run src/gateway-provider.test.ts` passes (90 tests). `pnpm
type-check` passes.
- oxfmt, ultracite, and `pnpm run-verifiers` pass.

commit.message:
fix(harness): abort a running turn when its host disconnects for good (#24611)

## background

when the host process dies for good mid turn (crash, deploy, killed
function), the bridge keeps the turn running in the sandbox with nobody
listening. it keeps calling tools and spending tokens until the turn
ends on its own or the sandbox stops (#23516)

## summary

- new `hostDisconnectTimeoutMs` option on the shared bridge (or the
`BRIDGE_HOST_DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` env). when the host's socket drops
mid turn and no host reconnects in time, the bridge aborts the turn the
same way an `abort` frame does
- a host that reconnects (`start` or `resume`) in time keeps the turn,
and a turn the host suspends on purpose is never aborted
- off by default, so nothing changes unless you set it
- claude code gets an opt-in `hostDisconnectTimeoutMs` setting that it
passes to the bridge. other adapters can opt in the same way later
- only a positive finite value turns it on. an invalid value like
`"20s"`, `NaN`, `0` or a negative number keeps the turn running instead
of aborting on every disconnect, and huge values are capped at the max
`setTimeout` delay
- docs on the claude code page

## verification

ran it in a vercel sandbox with real claude code, asked for 12 bash
calls that each append a tick and sleep 6s, then killed the host after
the 3rd

<details>
<summary>ticks after the host was killed</summary>

| | at kill | 20s after | 90s after | claude process |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no timeout (same as main) | 3 | 6 | 12 | kept running ~75s with no
host |
| `hostDisconnectTimeoutMs: 20000` | 3 | 6 | 6 | exited ~20s after the
kill |
| `hostDisconnectTimeoutMs: 'abc'` (invalid) | 3 | 6 | 12 | kept
running, same as main |

</details>

## checklist

- [x] tests have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] a _patch_ changeset for relevant packages has been added (run
`pnpm changeset` in root)
- [x] i have reviewed this pull request (self-review)

commit.message:
feat(anthropic): support message threads (#24397)

## Background

Anthropic's [message threads public
beta](https://claude.com/resources/articles/message-threads) lets active
conversations send only new messages on each Messages API request. This
reduces upload and preprocessing latency without changing token usage or
pricing.

## Summary

- Add native and Claude Platform on AWS support through typed
`providerOptions.anthropic.thread` create/continue options, map
`previousMessageId` to `previous_message_id`, and automatically include
the beta header.
- Omit the retained system prompt and tool definitions on continuation
while preserving tool conversion, tool choice, and per-request settings.
- Preserve thread error details in `APICallError.data` for
application-managed replay; reject message threads in batches and
incompatible compaction/context editing.
- Add generation and streaming examples, recovery guidance, regression
tests, and a patch changeset.

Conversation lifecycle stays explicit: applications retain their full
history, supply only new messages on continuation, and replay after
thread recovery errors. This does not add state to shared model
instances or introduce a core provider-spec abstraction.

API reference:
https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/message-threads

## End-to-End Verification

Built this checkout's local packages with:

```sh
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=ai... --filter=@ai-sdk/anthropic...
```

Using `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` configured in `examples/ai-functions/.env`,
ran the committed examples against the native Anthropic Messages API
with `claude-sonnet-4-6`:

```sh
cd examples/ai-functions
FAIL_ON_ERROR=1 node --import tsx src/generate-text/anthropic/message-threads.ts
FAIL_ON_ERROR=1 node --import tsx src/stream-text/anthropic/message-threads.ts
FAIL_ON_ERROR=1 node --import tsx src/agent/anthropic/message-threads.ts
```

The generation and streaming examples create a thread with a
favorite-color fact and continue with only a question. The second
response correctly recalled cobalt blue. The agent example completed two
steps, sending only the locally executed weather tool result on
continuation. Workspace links resolve `ai` and `@ai-sdk/anthropic` to
this checkout's built packages.

Also exercised the live API with a temporary script: a nonexistent
previous message ID returned `404` / `thread_not_found`, and a new
create request replaying the full history correctly answered the
question. A weather tool call was executed locally, then a continuation
containing only its tool result produced the final answer. Request
inspection confirmed `system` and `tools` were absent on continuation.
This verifies the recovery error path; natural five-minute expiration
and interrupted streams were not tested live.

## Validation

- `pnpm --filter @ai-sdk/anthropic test`: 865 tests passed in each of
Node and Edge runtimes.
- `pnpm --filter @ai-sdk/anthropic-aws test`: 62 tests passed in each of
Node and Edge runtimes.
- `pnpm type-check:full`: passed, including examples.
- `pnpm check`: passed.
- `pnpm verify:model-capabilities-docs`: passed.
- Compiled both changed provider documentation pages with the locally
installed `@mdx-js/mdx` compiler. Corrected the MDX type-annotation
parse failure found by the preview build.
- Critically reviewed with Claude Code CLI `--model opus` (resolved
model: `claude-opus-5-5`), using read-only tools. A second Opus review
confirmed the initial findings were addressed and identified the AWS
platform opt-in, which was then fixed.
- Addressed review findings in six separate logical, signed commits:
- `ab383b0a49`: fixed-setting guidance, beta pinning warnings/tests,
custom namespaces, JSON-tool continuation coverage.
- `2dc524bcd2`: preserve dynamic web-tool decoding; check interrupted
streams before continuation.
  - `f062ab12d7`: reject thread use on unsupported compatible platforms.
- `3cae07134e`: count top-level cache control, tolerate evolving error
details, identify unsupported batch requests.
- `42c9dfb3bf`: runnable ToolLoopAgent example and explicit pause,
fallback, refusal, and thinking replay guidance.
- `7de604029d`: follow-up review fix enabling the supported Claude
Platform on AWS provider, with tests and same-IAM-principal guidance.

### Scope and limitations

There is no automatic thread state or replay helper. Fixed fields and
beta sets must remain identical across turns; content-dependent beta
values must be pinned explicitly. `pause_turn` can be resumed through
the provider-level interface, while the high-level APIs currently reject
empty messages. Natural expiry, interrupted streams, and non-native
hosted platforms were not exercised live.

## Checklist

- [x] All commits are signed (PRs with unsigned commits cannot be
merged)
- [x] Tests have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] A _patch_ changeset for relevant packages has been added (for bug
fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root)
- [x] I have reviewed this pull request (self-review)

refactor(prodia): move model ID logic into a model catalog (#24552)

## Background

prodia's model capabilities and model-specific request policies were not
declared in a provider-owned catalog.

## Summary

Port prodia's model ID logic to a model catalog declaring capabilities,
provider option support, and request configuration while preserving
existing request behavior. Generate the provider capability tables and
option reference from that catalog.

Validation: existing Node and Edge tests passed (58 / 58 tests); package
build, type checking, formatting, and lint passed. Test files are
unchanged. Stacked on `aayush/207`.

## End-to-End Verification

Full-workspace `pnpm type-check:full` reports the existing error in the
unchanged Cartesia pronunciation-dictionary example:
`pronunciationDictionaryId` is not accepted by the current speech option
type. Provider package type checks passed.

Documentation generation and its stale-table check passed. No live
provider requests were made for this refactor. Existing provider
behavior was verified with the unchanged test suites; see validation
above.

<details>
<summary>Verification commands</summary>

```sh
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=@ai-sdk/prodia...
pnpm --filter @ai-sdk/prodia test
pnpm --filter @ai-sdk/prodia type-check
pnpm generate:model-capabilities-docs
pnpm verify:model-capabilities-docs
```
</details>
